title: Oskar investigates a theft
topic: A detective named Oskar investigates the theft of a necklace from a jewellery shop; a clerk remembers a stranger, muddy tracks lead into an alley, a delivery man confesses, Oskar solves the case before midnight
tail_E: The necklace is worth a fortune, because it is made of pure

author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (F12A, detective Oskar / theft)
notes: Formulation A. Ten meaning units: Oskar investigates a theft at a jewellery shop / the owner describes the stolen necklace / the display case stands open / a clerk remembers a stranger in a grey hat / Oskar finds muddy footprints / the trail leads into an alley / two neighbours hear noises after midnight / Oskar questions the clerk again / a delivery man admits the theft / Oskar solves the case. Subjects alternate between the protagonist (Oskar), other people (the owner, a clerk, two neighbours, a delivery man) and objects (the display case, the trail), singular and plural, so C3 switches cross real subject-verb agreement; units 3 and 6 have bare or copular intransitive predicates (stands open/steht offen, leads/führt). No separable German verbs ('zugeben', 'aufklären', 'abschließen' avoided in favour of 'gesteht' and 'löst'). 'Oskar' is the only proper name. Present tense and positive polarity throughout; unit 9 reads naturally in German, units 1 and 10 in English.
